title: Garden and Crown
premise: Lior Underhill, last apprentice of the Underhill smugglers' guild, discovers her name and today's date in the Thornfell Prophecies, a century-old text naming her the 'Crownless Bearer' who must carry a sealed seed of the old royal line through thirteen turns of the moon. Hunted by the king's inquisitors, a resurrected warlord who wants the seed as a weapon, and her own guild's ghosts, Lior learns the seed is not a claimant to the throne but a living record of every injustice the crown buried. In the end she refuses both throne and destruction: she plants the seed in the mountain's heart, where it grows into a tree whose roots expose the truth to all — justice delivered not by law or conquest, but by witness.
about_author: E. M. Nakamura is the pen name of a former cartographer's assistant who spent years mapping mountain passes before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people who live in the margins of empires, drawing on folklore gathered from border towns across three continents.

chapters.title: The Date That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Running contraband quills through Thornfell's smuggler roads, Lior shelters in an abandoned waystation and finds a prophecy book naming tonight's date — and her. The emotional beat: unease curdling into dread as the ink seems fresh on century-old paper.

chapters.title: What the Guild Buried
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She brings the book to her dying guildmaster, who confesses the Underhills have guarded the prophecy for generations and hands her a sealed iron seed hidden beneath the guildhall floor. Beat: grief and betrayal as family legacy becomes a burden.

chapters.title: Inquisitor Ash
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. The king's chief inquisitor arrives in the valley, burning waystations and interrogating smugglers, following the same prophecy. Beat: cold menace; we see Lior through hunter's eyes as a threat to order.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Fleeing with the seed, she deciphers the prophecy's terms: if she keeps it until the moon completes its thirteenth turn, something wakes; if she surrenders it, the war reignites either way. Beat: claustrophobic pressure of a ticking clock.

chapters.title: The Warlord Wakes
chapters.summary: Vessik's POV. A mercenary captain entombed since the old war stirs beneath the ice, drawn by the seed's awakening, and begins gathering the disaffected of the mountains. Beat: awe and horror; the stakes become ancient and personal at once.

chapters.title: Road of Thieves
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior bargains passage with rival smuggler clans who once scorned her dying guild, trading secrets for loyalty. Beat: tentative belonging; she discovers community among outcasts even as one clan betrays her location to Ash.

chapters.title: The Seed Speaks
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. On a high pass, the seed opens a sliver and floods Lior with memories: executions, famines, erased villages — the crown's buried crimes made living flesh. Beat: devastating empathy; she understands why the war nearly began.

chapters.title: Ash's Choice
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. Confronting Lior, Ash reads the seed's memories himself and recognizes his own family among the erased. Torn between oath and truth, he lets her go and burns his warrant. Beat: moral rupture; the law's servant defects to justice.

chapters.title: Crown of Ice and Root
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Vessik corners Lior at the mountain's heart on the thirteenth turn, offering her a throne built on the seed's power. Climax: Lior refuses, plants the seed in the deep stone, and its roots erupt, unmaking Vessik's borrowed army and binding him in living wood.

chapters.title: The Witness Tree
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, epilogue tone. A great tree now stands where no court sits, its leaves showing truths to all who touch them; smugglers, villagers, even reformed inquisitors gather beneath it. Lior, finally belonging somewhere, becomes its first keeper. Beat: quiet, earned hope.
